text:
mike: Quick heads upnoticed a goroutine leak in the Go SDK generator stream when user cancels ctx. Sample app hit it during timeout-heavy tests.

jess: Can you share the minimal repro + sdk version?

mike: repro attached, sdk v0.9.2. Steps: start GeneratorStream with context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second) and let it expire. Main goroutine returns, but a background retry goroutine persists. Snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  chunk, err := resp.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
// expected: no lingering goroutines after ctx cancel
```

mike: logs show repeated "stream read timeout" followed by a backoff loop spawning goroutines.

alex: Does the convenience GeneratorStream create an internal reconnect/backoff monitor? If so it might not be canceling on the user's ctx.

tomas: Correct — some helpers create an internal manager goroutine to handle reconnects and handshake. We probably didn't wire that to the request ctx.

mike: I grepped the code: backoff loop uses a parent service context, not the per-request ctx. So canceling user ctx doesn't stop it.

sandeep: Short-term mitigation: add an explicit Close() to the stream response that cancels internals. Long-term: make internals inherit the request ctx.
jess: Which is less risky to ship as a patch?

tomas: Add Close() now (non-breaking), then refactor to inherit ctx in a follow-up. We'll document both patterns.

mike: I tried a client-side workaround by selecting on ctx.Done() around Recv(), but that only exits the reader loop; the retry goroutine still lives. Example workaround:
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
    resp.Close()
    return ctx.Err()
  default:
    chunk, err := resp.Recv()
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
  }
}
```

jess: Please open a minimal failing test. I can run locally and add a goroutine-leak assertion.

mike: created tiny repo and test; `go test -run TestGenCancel -race` reproduces. gist: https://gist.example/xyz (sample + test).

ci-bot: CI for mike/gen-cancel-fix PR #789: 1 failed, 3 passed (leak test failed).

alex: Proposed implementation: export resp.Close() which cancels an internal cancelFunc used by retry/backoff goroutines. Also update examples with both ctx + Close patterns.

sandeep: I'll draft the PR. Plan: add Close() method, wire it to internal context, add unit test that ensures goroutine count returns to baseline, and docs snippet. Backport to 0.9.x after review.

jess: sounds good. ping @eng-runtime and @devex for fast review once PR is ready. Also add a short note in Go SDK migration guide about stream lifecycle.

mike: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/789 includes Close() + test + example.

ci-bot: PR 789 CI: running unit + e2e...

jess: thanks all. Closing thread; will reopen if post-merge flakiness shows up. :thumbsup:
